Emergency Room Patient Search

When Every Minute Counts, Patients Choose the ER They Find First

In an emergency, nobody browses. Patients and families search “ER near me”, tap the first trustworthy result on Maps, ask a voice assistant for the closest emergency room, and drive. Your ER must be instantly findable, clearly identified as a 24/7 emergency room, and impossible to confuse with an urgent care.

Why Your ER Must Be Ready on Every Platform

An emergency room has seconds, not minutes, to earn trust online. Wrong hours, a confusing entrance, or no clear “24/7 emergency room” signal can send a patient to another facility, and an AI assistant that can’t confirm your details simply won’t mention you.

  • GGoogle Maps & Search: 24/7 status, exact address, entrance and parking information must be accurate everywhere.
  • AIVoice & AI assistants: answer “closest ER open now” and “ER or urgent care?”. Clear, consistent facts make your ER the answer.
  • $Google Ads: captures emergency-intent searches when the landing page loads fast and shows call and directions first.
  • ★Reviews & social: families check reviews even in a hurry; recent, genuine feedback builds confidence.

ER marketing FAQ

Questions Emergency Room Leaders Ask

How do emergency rooms get more patients online?

Most ER patients come from Google Maps, local search and, increasingly, AI and voice assistants. Accurate 24/7 listings for every location, clear emergency positioning, fast mobile pages with call and directions first, genuine reviews and well-run Google Ads make the biggest difference.

Can a freestanding ER rank in AI answers like ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews?

Yes, when the ER is clearly described and consistent across the web: exact name, address and phone, 24/7 status, services, insurance information and accurate schema. No one can guarantee AI citations, but these steps make your ER a much stronger candidate.

How do you separate an ER from urgent care in search?

With correct Google Business Profile categories, explicit “24/7 emergency room” language, EmergencyService schema and transparent pages that explain when to choose an ER versus urgent care.

Do you run Google Ads for emergency rooms?

Yes. We build call-first, geo-targeted campaigns with conversion tracking and follow Google’s healthcare advertising policies.

How much does ER marketing cost?

Plans start at $750/month, with Basic at $1,250, Standard at $1,500 and Advanced from $2,000/month. There is no advance payment, no deposit and no long-term contract.

Do you work with ERs outside Texas?

Yes. WevTEC is Houston-based and has served clients nationwide since 2013. We won’t take on a direct competitor within your specific ZIP codes.
